extracted.intended_audience: registrants, corporate accountants, auditors, and securities lawyers preparing SEC registration/proxy/IPO filings
extracted.subtask_short: SEC reporting for real estate acquisitions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on SEC financial statement and disclosure requirements when a registrant acquires businesses generally and real estate operations specifically, including significance tests, periods to present, pro forma preparation, and special rules for combinations under common control and IPOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance tests for acquisitions (asset, income, investment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the significance of an acquired business by applying the three tests (asset, income and investment tests) in Rule 1-02(w) / Rule 3-05; for acquired real estate operations, apply only the investment test under S-X Rule 3-14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculations compare financial data of registrant and acquiree for the fiscal years most recently completed prior to the acquisition. Use pro forma consolidated amounts where required; assets and pretax income of acquired businesses should reflect any new cost basis from purchase accounting. (Example: an acquisition measured 55% by asset-test may measure 22% when registrant financials are restated as-if pooled.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of parent entity and predecessor for common-control combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: For combinations of entities under common control, first identify the parent entity that controls the entities being combined; then determine the predecessor (normally the entity first controlled by the parent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although parent financial statements are not required in the registration statement, identifying the parent affects accounting in the combined financial statements. The predecessor provides the same financial statements as a registrant would (full financial statements for all periods as required under S-X Rules 3-01/3-02 or 8-02/8-03). The predecessor is not eligible for relief under S-X Rule 3-05 for an acquired business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial registration statements for combinations under common control
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing an initial registration statement after a common-control combination, present audited financial statements of the combined company for required periods, adjusting historical financials retrospectively to reflect the as-if pooling-of-interests method where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significance of prior acquisitions should be determined using the registrant's adjusted as-if pooled financial statements (e.g., restated total assets used in asset-test). The initial registration statement must contain the audited financial statements of the combined company for the required years (three years in examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: SAB 80 application and staff guidance for IPOs built by aggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: For initial public offerings involving businesses built by aggregation of discrete businesses that remain substantially intact, staff may measure significance against the combined entities that will comprise the registrant at the filing date rather than at the acquisition date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy intends to ensure the registration statement includes at least three, two and one years of audited financial statements for not less than 60%, 80% and 90%, respectively, of constituent businesses. The staff permits measuring the significance tests against combined pro forma entities. SAB 80 relief exists but may be rare after 2021 amendments to Rule 3-05; consider carefully with auditors and counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for omitting pre-acquisition audited financial statements (SAB 80 thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-acquisition audited financial statements of an acquiree may be omitted from the registration statement only if certain combined-significance conditions are met based on the length of the audited-period presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The combined significance of businesses for which audited financial statements cover a period of less than: (a) 9 months may not exceed 10%; (b) 21 months may not exceed 20%; (c) 33 months may not exceed 40%. Combined significance is the sum of each included company's highest computed significance level under the three tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro forma financial statement preparation and application (Article 11 guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro forma financial information must be prepared consistent with Article 11: the pro forma balance sheet should be as of the registrant’s latest balance sheet date included in the filing and give effect to acquisitions as if acquired on that date; the pro forma statement of operations should be for the registrant’s most recent fiscal year included and give effect to acquisitions as if consummated at the beginning of that fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pro forma tests should reflect acquisitions consummated during and subsequent to the year and probable acquisitions; pro forma amounts used for significance must reflect transaction accounting adjustments and may not be created by annualizing data. If pro forma amounts are used to determine significance, the registrant must continue to use pro forma amounts to determine significance of acquisitions and dispositions through the filing date of its next annual report.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-X Rule 3-14: definition and scope of a 'real estate operation'
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'real estate operation' is a business that generates substantially all of its revenues through the leasing of real property; the acquisition includes interests accounted for by the equity method or fair value option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquisitions of groups of related real estate operations that are probable or have occurred after the registrant's latest fiscal year-end will be treated as a single acquisition and may be presented on a combined basis for periods under common control/management. Rule 3-14 does not apply to a real estate operation totally held by the registrant prior to the transaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods to be presented for acquired real estate operations (Rule 3-14 investment test thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether financial statements of an acquired real estate operation must be filed and for which periods using the modified investment-test thresholds: if the condition does not exceed 20% no statements are required; if it exceeds 20% file at least the most recent fiscal year and most recent interim period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the aggregate impact of acquired or to-be-acquired real estate operations since the date of the registrant's most recent audited balance sheet exceeds 50%, the registrant must provide pro forma financial information and statements covering at least the most recent fiscal year and interim period for acquired operations not yet required. The investment test should include assumed debt secured by the real properties when the registrant uses consolidated total assets as the denominator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission relief and timing for filing omitted real estate operation statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration statements and proxy statements need not include separate financial statements of an acquired real estate operation if neither the operation nor aggregate impact exceeds the modified 50%/20% significance conditions and certain timing conditions are met (e.g., consummation not occurred or final prospectus date within 74 days after consummation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A registrant (other than certain foreign private issuers) that omits required statements must file those financial statements and any required pro forma information on Form 8-K no later than 75 days after consummation. Separate financial statements need not be presented once operating results have been reflected in the registrant's audited consolidated financial statements for at least nine months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation format for abbreviated financial statements of real estate operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviated financial statements for a real estate operation may consist only of statements of revenues and expenses excluding expenses not comparable to proposed future operations (e.g., mortgage interest, leasehold rental, depreciation, amortization, corporate overhead, income taxes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes must disclose (i) the type of omitted expenses and reasons for exclusion; (ii) how the presented financials are not indicative of future operations because of omitted expenses; and (iii) information about operating, investing and financing cash flows to the extent available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental disclosures describing material factors for real estate operations
rubrics_metrics.description: For each real estate operation requiring financial statements, material factors considered by the registrant in assessing the operation must be described with specificity in the filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosures should include sources of revenue (competition in rental market, comparative rents, occupancy rates) and expense (utility rates, property tax rates, maintenance expenses, anticipated capital improvements). The disclosure must also indicate the registrant is not aware of any other material factors that would cause the reported financial statements not to be indicative of future operating results. (Instruction: when presented in Form S-11, supplement Item 15 disclosures.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro forma filing triggers per S-X Rule 11-01
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro forma financial information must be filed when specified conditions exist, such as a significant business acquisition during the most recent fiscal year, consummation of a significant acquisition or common-control combination after the latest balance sheet, securities to be offered to security holders of a significant business, significant dispositions, roll-up transactions, registrant formerly part of another entity, or other material transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A business acquisition or disposition will be considered significant under Rule 11-01 if it meets the definition of a significant subsidiary with 20% substituted for 10% (and real estate operations follow the modified investment-test guidance in Rule 3-14). The determination should generally use the registrant's most recent annual consolidated financial statements and the business's pre-acquisition financial statements for the same fiscal year, unless allowed alternatives (e.g., specified pro forma amounts or certain S-X 3-05 presentations) are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and limitations of pro forma amounts to determine significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance tests may be made using pro forma amounts that depict the aggregate impact of acquisitions and dispositions consummated after the latest fiscal year-end, but such pro forma amounts must follow Article 11 rules and may not be created by annualizing data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using pro forma amounts to determine significance: (a) the registrant must have filed audited financial statements for acquired businesses for required periods and required pro forma information for such businesses; (b) continue using pro forma amounts to determine significance through the filing date of the next annual report; and (c) pro forma amounts should only depict significant acquisitions/dispositions and include Transaction Accounting Adjustments as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment-test calculation detail when using consolidated assets denominator
rubrics_metrics.description: When the investment test is based on the registrant's consolidated total assets, include any assumed debt secured by the real properties in the 'investments in' the tested real estate operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination must be made using the prescribed definitions and methods in §210.11-01(b)(3) and (4); consider capital structure anomalies and whether alternative calculations or accommodations are appropriate per guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of related real estate operations as a single acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisitions of a group of related real estate operations that are probable or have occurred after the latest fiscal year-end will be treated as a single acquisition for purposes of Rule 3-14 and may be presented on a combined basis for periods under common control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operations are related if (i) under common control or management; (ii) acquisition of one is conditional on acquisition of each other; or (iii) each acquisition is conditioned on a single common event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign real estate operation financial statement accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements of an acquired foreign real estate operation that meet Item 17 of Form 20-F may satisfy Rule 3-14; such statements may be reconciled to U.S. GAAP or prepared under IFRS-IASB where applicable with specific reconciliation rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign private issuers preparing under IFRS may use IFRS without reconciliation to U.S. GAAP in some situations; reconciliations generally follow Item 17(c) of Form 20-F but accommodations inconsistent with IFRS-IASB may not be applied. If a real estate operation would be a foreign private issuer, statements may be prepared in another comprehensive basis of accounting and reconciled to IFRS or U.S. GAAP per the specified rules.
